subject: Second-order latent factor growth curve models: Fixing the factor loadings vs. fixing the variances of the latent variables

messages.author: eaf891916146cc5e
messages.subject: Second-order latent factor growth curve models: Fixing the factor loadings vs. fixing the variances of the latent variables
parts:
Hi everyone,

I fitted a second-order latent factor growth curve model. The first order is a bi-factor model with four general factors (on_maintenance_numerical, on_maintenance_spatial, off_maintenance_numerical, and off_maintenance_spatial,) and two specific factors (on_intcontrol and off_intcontrol). The second order is a growth curve model in which the intercept and the slope act on the two specific factors. Strong measurement invariance is modeled. Here is the model:

## Cutting-edge alternative - multivariate growth curve modeling

m <- '# multivariate growth curve modeling

# 1. First order latent variables - bi-factor model  (weak invariance)

on_maintenance_numerical =~  b10*on_csnumerical + b1*on_updatingnumerical + b2*on_ssnumerical + b3*on_ssverbal

on_maintenance_spatial =~ b11*on_csspatial +  b4*on_updatingspatial + b5*on_ssspatial + b6*on_ssarrow

on_intcontrol =~  b12*on_csnumerical + b7*on_csspatial + b8*on_updatingnumerical + b9*on_updatingspatial

off_maintenance_numerical =~  b10*off_csnumerical + b1*off_updatingnumerical + b2*off_ssnumerical + b3*off_ssverbal

off_maintenance_spatial =~ b11*off_csspatial +  b4*off_updatingspatial + b5*off_ssspatial + b6*off_ssarrow

off_intcontrol =~  b12*off_csnumerical + b7*off_csspatial + b8*off_updatingnumerical + b9*off_updatingspatial

#2. Fixing the reference indicators’ intercepts at zero

on_csnumerical ~ 0*1

on_csspatial ~ 0*1

off_csnumerical ~ 0*1

off_csspatial ~ 0*1

#3. Do not estimate (i.e. fix at zero) the first-order latent variable means

on_maintenance_numerical ~ 0*1

on_maintenance_spatial ~ 0*1

on_intcontrol ~ 0*1

off_maintenance_numerical ~ 0*1

off_maintenance_spatial ~ 0*1

off_intcontrol ~ 0*1

#4. Constrain the other indicators’ intercepts to strong time equivalence (invariance)

on_updatingnumerical ~ w1*1

on_ssnumerical ~ w2*1

on_ssverbal ~ w3*1

on_updatingspatial ~ w4*1

on_ssspatial ~ w5*1

on_ssarrow ~ w6*1

off_updatingnumerical ~ w1*1

off_ssnumerical ~ w2*1

off_ssverbal ~ w3*1

off_updatingspatial ~ w4*1

off_ssspatial ~ w5*1

off_ssarrow ~ w6*1

#5.1 Measurement error autocorrelations

on_ssnumerical ~~ off_ssnumerical

on_ssverbal ~~ off_ssverbal

on_ssspatial ~~ off_ssspatial

on_ssarrow ~~ off_ssarrow

on_csnumerical ~~ off_csnumerical

on_updatingnumerical ~~ off_updatingnumerical

on_csspatial ~~ off_csspatial

on_updatingspatial ~~ off_updatingspatial

#5.2 Fix to zero latent correlations because of bi-factor modeling

on_maintenance_numerical ~~ 0*on_intcontrol

on_maintenance_spatial ~~ 0*on_intcontrol

off_maintenance_numerical ~~ 0*off_intcontrol

off_maintenance_spatial ~~ 0*off_intcontrol

on_maintenance_numerical ~~ 0*off_intcontrol

on_maintenance_spatial ~~ 0*off_intcontrol

off_maintenance_numerical ~~ 0*on_intcontrol

off_maintenance_spatial ~~ 0*on_intcontrol

#6. Second-order factors of the linear model

i_intcontrol =~ 1*off_intcontrol + 1*on_intcontrol

s_intcontrol =~ 0*off_intcontrol + 1*on_intcontrol

i_maintenance_numerical =~ 1*off_maintenance_numerical + 1*on_maintenance_numerical

s_maintenance_numerical =~ 0*off_maintenance_numerical + 1*on_maintenance_numerical

i_maintenance_spatial =~ 1*off_maintenance_spatial + 1*on_maintenance_spatial

s_maintenance_spatial =~ 0*off_maintenance_spatial + 1*on_maintenance_spatial

# 6.2 Fix to zero the correlations between the first-order factors, the slope and intercept factors

on_intcontrol ~~ 0*i_maintenance_numerical

on_intcontrol ~~ 0*s_maintenance_numerical

on_intcontrol ~~ 0*i_maintenance_spatial

on_intcontrol ~~ 0*s_maintenance_spatial

on_maintenance_numerical ~~ 0*i_intcontrol

on_maintenance_numerical ~~ 0*s_intcontrol

on_maintenance_numerical ~~ 0*i_maintenance_spatial

on_maintenance_numerical ~~ 0*s_maintenance_spatial

on_maintenance_spatial ~~ 0*i_intcontrol

on_maintenance_spatial ~~ 0*s_intcontrol

on_maintenance_spatial ~~ 0*i_maintenance_numerical

on_maintenance_spatial ~~ 0*s_maintenance_numerical

off_intcontrol ~~ 0*i_maintenance_numerical

off_intcontrol ~~ 0*s_maintenance_numerical

off_intcontrol ~~ 0*i_maintenance_spatial

off_intcontrol ~~ 0*s_maintenance_spatial

off_maintenance_numerical ~~ 0*i_intcontrol

off_maintenance_numerical ~~ 0*s_intcontrol

off_maintenance_numerical ~~ 0*i_maintenance_spatial

off_maintenance_numerical ~~ 0*s_maintenance_spatial

off_maintenance_spatial ~~ 0*i_intcontrol

off_maintenance_spatial ~~ 0*s_intcontrol

off_maintenance_spatial ~~ 0*i_maintenance_numerical

off_maintenance_spatial ~~ 0*s_maintenance_numerical

'

First, I fitted the model by fixing to 1 the factor loadings of the first indicator of each latent variable. To this end, I used the following code:

fit <- lavaan::growth(m, data = tmp)

In this case, I got the following warning message:

Warnings:

I have the following questions:

1. Why do the results differ across both modeling approaches?

Please note that I tried to fix to 1 the variances of the latent variables in the model. That is, I added in the model:

“on_maintenance_numerical ~~ 1*on_maintenance_numerical

  off_maintenance_numerical ~~ 1*off_maintenance_numerical

  on_maintenance_spatial ~~ 1*on_maintenance_spatial

  off_maintenance_spatial ~~ 1*off_maintenance_spatial

  on_intcontrol ~~ 1*on_intcontrol

  off_intcontrol ~~ 1*off_intcontrol

  i_intcontrol ~~ 1*i_intcontrol

  s_intcontrol ~~ 1*s_intcontrol”

 

In this case, I got  the following warning message:

Warnings:

In lav_object_post_check(object) :

  lavaan WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negative

 

Moreover, when only the bi-factor model is assessed either by fixing to 1 the factor loadings of the first indicator of each latent variable or by fixing to 1 the variances of all the latent variables with std.lv = TRUE, the results are similar.

 

2. In the second modeling approach, some standardized coefficients are above 1 (see the highlighted values in the results section). Why is this the case?

 

Thanks in advance for your help!

Best,
Alodie

messages.subject: Re: Second-order latent factor growth curve models: Fixing the factor loadings vs. fixing the variances of the latent variables
parts: 1. Why do the results differ across both modeling approaches?
2. In the second modeling approach, some standardized coefficients are above 1 (see the highlighted values in the results section). Why is this the case?

Those are standardized intercepts.  They are not bound within 1.  They are just intercepts expressed in units of SD.

Hi Terrence,

Thank you for your response, and sorry that my previous message was not clear.

With both approaches, I mean the way of reducing the number of parameters to be estimated. That is:
  1. approach 1: fixing to 1 the factor loadings of the first indicator of each latent variable 
    • In this case, I used the following code: fit <- lavaan::growth(m, data = tmp)
      and I got some warnings:

• Warnings:

      1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :

        lavaan WARNING:

          The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov)

          does not appear to be positive definite! The smallest eigenvalue

          (= 2.467171e-14) is close to zero. This may be a symptom that the

          model is not identified.

      2: In lav_object_post_check(object) :

        lavaan WARNING: some estimated lv variances are negative

2. approach 2: fixing to 1 the variances of all the latent variables. 
    • In this case, I used the following code: fit <- lavaan::growth(m, data = tmp, std.lv = TRUE)
      and I got a model with acceptable fit statistics

For me, it is unclear why the results are different. I suppose that this has something to do with the second-order growth curve aspect of the model. When only fitting the bi-factor model (first order), the results are simialr across both approches.

Best,
Alodie

messages.subject: Re: Second-order latent factor growth curve models: Fixing the factor loadings vs. fixing the variances of the latent variables
parts: For me, it is unclear why the results are different.
Different scaling methods should yield identical fit, but the parameter estimates will differ proportional to the change in scale.
I suppose that this has something to do with the second-order growth curve aspect of the model.

Probably.  The growth() wrapper is designed for growth factors with observed indicators, but that is not the model you are trying to fit.  I would use the cfa() or sem() wrappers (identical default ?lavOptions) or simply specify every nonzero parameter in your syntax so you can use the bare-bones lavaan() function.  Either way, check your parTable() to see whether you are fixing/estimating what you intend to.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
